title: Lime Growers of Papantla, Veracruz, Will Export to Russia for the First Time; It Will Be 21.4 Tons of the Citrus
author: Jared Laureles and Alexia Villaseñor
content:
_This article by Jared Laureles and Alexia Villaseñor originally appeared in
the[July 2, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/07/02/sociedad/limoneros-de-
papantla-veracruz-exportaran-por-primera-vez-a-rusia-seran-214-toneladas-del-
citrico), Mexico's premier left wing daily newspaper._

Growers from Papantla, Veracruz, finalized the first export of 21.4 tons of
Persian lime to Russia, after their crops reached the maturity and quality
standards required for that market, the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural
Development (Sader) reported. It noted that the export volume could increase
to 257.4 tons during the second half of 2026, which would strengthen the
presence of Mexican citrus in the Eurasian market.

Papantla has at least 9,500 producers with the capacity to supply Persian
lime. The geography of its territory allows cultivation from sea level up to
1,600 meters of altitude, "which guarantees continuous supply, compensating
for climatic difficulties such as droughts," it elaborated.

The agency highlighted that the Veracruz citrus stood out to international
buyers for its long shelf life –indispensable for withstanding the sea journey
of more than 30 days–, exceptional physical quality –with an intense green
color, a size suited to the European market, and the required peel roughness–
and because the crops are between 3 and 5 years old.

"The growers foresee that this first step will open a range of new
opportunities for the region, since that figure could rise to 257.4 tons in
the next six months," it said.

Sader attributed the result to the direct-marketing strategy promoted by its
head, Columba López, with strategic projects such as lime, vanilla, cacao,
coffee, achiote, and orange during her tenure as national coordinator of the
Sembrando Vida program.

The tools allowed the farmers to "add value to their harvests and, above all,
negotiate directly with foreign businesspeople" during world-class agri-food
fairs such as Biofach (Nuremberg) and Fruit Logística (Berlin), both in
Germany, where they took part by holding certifications or sustainable
agroecological practices, it indicated.
